description: Prompt Navigator - A comprehensive guide offering core AI prompting techniques with examples tailored for college faculty.

coreTechniques.name: Zero-Shot Prompting
coreTechniques.useWhen: You want a quick baseline answer or definition without providing examples.
coreTechniques.definition: Zero-shot prompting asks the AI to perform a task without any examples in the prompt. You give a direct instruction or question and the model responds using its general training. It's the fastest way to get an initial draft, explanation, or list because you don't have to prepare demonstrations or special formatting ahead of time.
coreTechniques.useCase: Use for fast definitions, quick contrasts, or rapid lists. In class prep, it's a handy way to draft a first pass that you can refine with follow-ups.
coreTechniques.whenWhy: When you need a quick baseline, when preparing early drafts, or when exploring unfamiliar topics.
examplePrompts: Explain the concept of social stratification in simple terms for an intro sociology class (~120 words) and include one concrete, everyday example.
List the three most important differences between photosynthesis and cellular respiration in a single paragraph for first-year students.

coreTechniques.name: Few-Shot Prompting
coreTechniques.useWhen: The output must match a specific format, tone, or rubric.
coreTechniques.definition: Few-shot prompting includes one or more examples of the task and desired output inside the prompt. The model uses these demonstrations to infer structure, tone, and level, then produces a new response that mirrors the pattern.
coreTechniques.useCase: Provide an example student answer with model feedback, then ask for feedback on a new answer in the same style. Or show two well-formed quiz items and request five new items that match difficulty and structure.
coreTechniques.whenWhy: Reach for few-shot when zero-shot was generic, when format is critical, or when you need a stable voice. Good examples = better outputs; 1-3 concise demos are usually enough.

coreTechniques.name: System & Role Prompts
coreTechniques.useWhen: You need consistent behavior, constraints, or a specific persona.
coreTechniques.definition: System and role prompts set global instructions or a persona that persists across the conversation. A system prompt defines boundaries, while a role prompt assigns a character or expertise level.

coreTechniques.name: Context Injection
coreTechniques.useWhen: Outputs must follow your local readings, rubrics, levels, or constraints.
coreTechniques.definition: Context injection means pasting relevant material directly into the prompt. The AI then grounds its response in your specific content rather than relying on general training data.

coreTechniques.name: Step-Back Prompting
coreTechniques.useWhen: You want the model to identify the problem type and plan before solving.
coreTechniques.definition: Step-back prompting asks the AI to pause before answering, identify the underlying type of problem, and outline an approach or plan.

coreTechniques.name: Chain-of-Thought Prompting
coreTechniques.useWhen: The reasoning steps themselves are instructional or must be checked.
coreTechniques.definition: Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting instructs the AI to show its work - explaining each reasoning step before giving the final answer.

coreTechniques.name: Self-Consistency
coreTechniques.useWhen: Single-run outputs vary and you need a more reliable result.
coreTechniques.definition: Self-consistency asks the AI to generate multiple independent answers to the same question, then compare them.

coreTechniques.name: Tree-of-Thought Prompting
coreTechniques.useWhen: There are multiple viable approaches and you want options before deciding.
coreTechniques.definition: Tree-of-thought (ToT) prompting asks the AI to explore multiple solution paths in parallel before evaluating and recommending the best one.

coreTechniques.name: ReAct (Reason & Act)
coreTechniques.useWhen: The task benefits from alternating reasoning with actions or questions.
coreTechniques.definition: ReAct prompting structures the AI's process as a loop: Reason about what it knows and what's missing, Act by asking a clarifying question or performing a sub-task, then Observe the result before continuing.

commonProblems.description: Prompts without context produce generic results.
commonProblems.fix: Include course level, focus, and objectives.

commonProblems.description: Without stating learner level or background, AI may pitch content too high or low.

commonProblems.fix: State the format and desired length.

commonProblems.description: Multiple tasks in one prompt can confuse the AI.
commonProblems.fix: Break requests into smaller, sequential prompts.

commonProblems.description: Without guidance, tone and style may be off.
commonProblems.fix: Assign a role to anchor the voice.

commonProblems.description: First outputs can contain errors or bias.
commonProblems.fix: Review, refine, and verify before use.

workflowSteps.title: Define Your Goal
workflowSteps.description: Be specific about the task and purpose.

workflowSteps.title: Add Context
workflowSteps.description: Include audience, course level, content source, and constraints.

workflowSteps.title: Draft Clearly
workflowSteps.description: Keep it one cohesive request; split complex tasks.

workflowSteps.title: Test
workflowSteps.description: Run it and check for accuracy, tone, and format.

workflowSteps.title: Spot Gaps
workflowSteps.description: Identify missing details, wrong tone, or off-target content.

workflowSteps.title: Refine
workflowSteps.description: Adjust scope, tone, format, and add examples if needed.

workflowSteps.title: Iterate
workflowSteps.description: Test and tweak until results consistently meet expectations.

workflowSteps.title: Document
workflowSteps.description: Save the final prompt for reuse or sharing.
